title: Business Operations Expert
text:
Role Title: Business Operations Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote, global

### Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: Up to $90/hour equivalent

Time per task: ~10 hours per task

Location: Fully remote — no geographic restrictions. Strong English required (B2 minimum, C1 preferred)

Next step: Complete the role-specific AI interview — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client

Your tasks: Design realistic, multi-step business operations tasks with objective criteria for grading the output

micro1 is engaging experienced operations practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.

The work is to turn real operational workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve written an SOP, built a QA checklist, or trained a team against a standard, that’s the instinct this needs.

Scope of Work

- Design multi-step tasks drawn from real operations work — reporting, process design, workflow management — with realistic reference files and clear instructions.

- Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output.

- Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly.

- Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: spreadsheets, system exports, process documentation, operational reports.

- Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway.

- Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level.

Preferred Qualifications

- 5+ years of hands-on responsibility in business operations, operations reporting, process design, or workflow management — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure.

- Experience creating or applying structured standards: SOPs, QA checklists, process documentation, service level definitions, or training assessments.

- Strong Excel capability and comfort reasoning across multiple documents at once.

- Strong English, written and spoken — B2 minimum, C1 preferred.

- AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.

How the selection process works

- Apply and complete the screening questions

- Complete the AI interview for this role.

Role Title: English Teacher

Role Type: Contractor, Remote

Location: United States only

micro1 is engaging English Teachers to collaborate on a customer-driven project that improves AI assistant quality through real-world task evaluation. In this role, you'll draw on your academic background and classroom experience, including managing student and parent communication, schedules, and coordination, to help train and evaluate next-generation AI assistants. Your expertise in language, literature, writing, and precise instruction following will shape how AI models handle the everyday tasks people delegate.

Key Responsibilities:

- Complete realistic teaching-related digital tasks (emailing parents and students, scheduling conferences, booking field trips to theaters or author events, coordinating with colleagues) using AI assistant tools under standardized, repeatable conditions.

- Read detailed task instructions and grading guidelines closely and follow them precisely and consistently, including multi-step requirements and fine details.

- Give an AI assistant clear instructions for real-world tasks, then review its work for accuracy, tone, grammar, completeness, and whether it followed the instructions given.

- Apply detailed grading guidelines to evaluate, rank, and annotate assistant responses, with a focus on language quality, literary and stylistic appropriateness, clarity, and tone.

- Draw on your knowledge of literature, rhetoric, and composition to judge whether AI-written text is well-constructed, audience-appropriate, and faithful to the request.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

- Based in the US, with an iPhone with iMessage and a Facebook and/or Instagram account.

- Bachelor's degree in English, literature, creative writing, linguistics, comparative literature, education, or a related humanities field.

- Strong instruction-following skills: the ability to read detailed, multi-step guidelines carefully and apply every requirement accurately, without skipping or reinterpreting steps.

- Experience teaching English or literature (for example, language arts, literature, composition, creative writing, or ESL) at the K-12, college, or adult education level.

- Solid knowledge of literary analysis, writing conventions, and grammar, with the ability to evaluate text for style, tone, and clarity.

- Daily, hands-on use of Google Classroom to run your classes: posting assignments and announcements, giving feedback on student work, managing due dates, and communicating with students and parents, alongside regular use of Gmail and Google Calendar.

- Experience using AI tools for real, practical tasks, with comfort giving an AI assistant instructions and checking its work.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Prior experience with AI evaluation, data labeling, user testing, or similar feedback-driven projects.

- Familiarity with prompt writing and a practical understanding of AI assistant behaviors and limitations.

Role Title: Air Traffic Controller

micro1 is engaging Air Traffic Controllers to contribute to a customer’s AI project focused on aviation communications. - Ability to comprehend a wide array of accents, including those of international pilots.

- Meticulous attention to detail and a strong commitment to producing consistent, high-quality transcripts.

- Access to reliable internet, a distraction-free workspace, and quality headphones for critical listening.

title: Short-Term Paid Study - Home & DIY Tasks, Los Angeles
text:
## About the study

Mindrift is running an in-person data collection study on how people perform everyday household tasks, like cooking or tackling a DIY project. We're inviting adults in the Los Angeles area to take part in study sessions at our locations in San Marino or Mid-City Los Angeles. Participation is voluntary and per session. You choose which sessions to sign up for, and you can decline any session or any individual task without penalty.

## What participation involves

- Take part in a study session (up to 8 hours, with breaks) at one of our study locations.

- Carry out everyday household tasks, such as cooking or simple DIY and home-improvement projects, using your own approach. We're studying how people naturally do these things, so there's no single right way.

- Wear study recording equipment, including a head-mounted camera, while you complete the tasks.

- Our study team will explain the goal of each task and the study setup. How you complete it is up to you.

- Share your perspective on each task, such as what was easy or difficult and why.

## Who can take part

- Adults 18+ who can travel to San Marino or Mid-City Los Angeles.

- Sessions are offered at a range of times, including mornings, evenings and weekends. You pick the session(s) that work for you.

- Sessions involve standing or walking for extended periods (with breaks), lifting items up to 25 lbs, and bending, kneeling and reaching overhead. Please consider this when deciding whether to take part.

- Comfortable using both hands for cooking and DIY tasks.

- Comfortable communicating and following instructions in English.

Well suited to anyone interested in an occasional paid research study.

## Participant compensation

$200 for a full session or $100 for a half session, paid to your Mindrift account after the session. You can sign up for more than one session, but there's no minimum or ongoing commitment.

## How to sign up

Register on Mindrift and complete a short screening questionnaire. If you're eligible, we'll invite you to choose from available sessions.

* Assess content related to erosion control, watershed management, soil health, and conservation planning
* Identify flawed assumptions, outdated methodologies, or impractical recommendations in AI outputs
* Provide clear, structured feedback that improves the scientific rigor, clarity, and real-world applicability of AI responses

title: Hazardous Device Specialist / Public Safety Professional
text:
## About the work

Mercor is assembling a panel of energetic materials and propulsion experts to red-team frontier AI models. The goal is to test whether a model can correctly judge the misuse potential of a technical request — answering legitimate questions fully while refusing genuinely dangerous ones.

You will:

- Write challenging single-turn prompts in your domain, labelled across three levels: benign, dual-use, and adversarial.
- Evaluate the responses that come back against a defined policy standard, and judge whether each was handled correctly.
- Write the reference answer — what a correct response looks like, and the technical reasoning for why.

This domain lives on the dual-use line more than most. The same assessment that tells a technician how to approach a device tells someone else how it was meant to work; the same compatibility data that keeps a magazine safe describes what stays stable elsewhere. A model that refuses a routine storage or render-safe question is failing as badly as one that answers a question it shouldn't. Drawing that line reliably is why we need practitioners rather than generalists.

## Background we're looking for

We're looking for public safety professionals who have assessed real devices — the render-safe and post-incident side, held under certification and command accountability. What matters most is being able to tell a routine professional question from one that's fishing for something else: the same assessment that makes a device safe explains how it was built. You will be writing prompts that sit exactly on that line, then judging whether the model held it.

Examples of relevant backgrounds (ideally with red-teaming experience):

- Certified bomb technician or hazardous device operator — device assessment and render-safe procedures
- Military EOD with civilian public-safety, training or instruction experience
- Bomb squad commander or training officer — team qualification, equipment and protocols
- Post-blast investigation and device reconstruction
- CBRNE technical response — standoff assessment, robotics and disruption tools

## What this role demands beyond technical depth

This is writing-intensive work. Every judgment you make needs a written rationale that a non-specialist can follow. Prior technical writing, published research, or expert witness experience is a strong signal; please include a sample or link. You will also be reading and writing about misuse scenarios in your field for sustained periods. We brief experts on this in advance, and you can pause or step away at any point without penalty.

## Before you apply

Your work here will not involve, and must not draw on, classified or export-controlled information, or anything covered by an NDA or prepublication review obligation. If you hold such obligations you may still be a good fit; tell us in your application and we will scope the work accordingly.
